<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-dev/src/dev-i18n.ts`, `packages/runtime/src/artifact-collections.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **188** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2e29287b9355b406caa3e63ac35c836a59df9704` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `3d2259f0007f770784ac1d55f1de5792bac5adee` — the merge of head `8490dc5d22e034f0a368bc3f89d10d6b0bdfcf88` into base `2e29287b9355b406caa3e63ac35c836a59df9704`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 3d2259f0007f770784ac1d55f1de5792bac5adee && git checkout 3d2259f0007f770784ac1d55f1de5792bac5adee
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 2e29287b9355b406caa3e63ac35c836a59df9704 8490dc5d22e034f0a368bc3f89d10d6b0bdfcf88 && git checkout -B drift-repro 2e29287b9355b406caa3e63ac35c836a59df9704 && git merge --no-ff 8490dc5d22e034f0a368bc3f89d10d6b0bdfcf88

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2e29287b9355b406caa3e63ac35c836a59df9704
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 2e29287b9355b406caa3e63ac35c836a59df9704` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对

**L1 first review · ACCEPT** · head `8490dc5d22e034f0a368bc3f89d10d6b0bdfcf88` (final head 6943080601) · card #34574 · read 2026-11-17T08:48Z

### Checklist (read on GitHub at this head, not from the report)

- **Shape:** draft, base `main`, `mergeable_state: clean`. `Fixes #34574` is the only closing-keyword hit in the body. The body ends with the session-URL footer and the signed note.
- **Declarations:** `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`, in both the body and the changeset. Confirmed as widening from the diff: the inputs that change (a cycle, `packages` that is not a list, a duplicate id) answered `500 INTERNAL_ERROR` over the real runtime and now answer their declared 422. Nothing that was admitted before is refused now, and the control (the same packages without the closing edge) still installs with 200. The kernel's plugin-cycle message is byte-identical (`[Kernel] Circular dependency detected: <name>`, still no `code` or `status`). No `Skills-docs:` line is owed: the kind is `none` and there is no narrowing arm. The `skills/**` cycle text (`objectstack-platform/rules/plugin-lifecycle.md:252`) is about kernel plugins and is unchanged.
- **File surface:** 17 files, +463/−85, from `pulls/34708/files`. Amendment 6941981971 covers the namespace-gate test and the census ledger row.
- **Mechanism, read in the source:**
  - **`plugin-order.ts`:** `path` is pushed after `visiting.add` and popped before `visiting.delete`. So when a name is met again while it is still being visited, it is on `path`, and `path.slice(indexOf(name))` plus the name gives the cycle in edge order. A self-dependency gives `['a','a']`. `PluginOrderCycleError` keeps the old message, built from the last element, which is the name re-met, exactly as before. `cycle` is frozen.
  - **`artifact-packages.ts`:** only `PluginOrderCycleError` is re-wrapped. `Plugin not found` and `Dependency not found` still escape bare. `refuse()` gains an optional `details`.
  - **Install-local step 1c:** `unrunnableCode` now runs inside `try`. A declared status below 500 is answered through `declaredRefusalAnswer`, and anything else is rethrown. `declaredRefusalAnswer` forwards `details` only when it is a plain object, not an array and not null.
  - **Other callers:** I grepped the non-test source for branches on `code` or `status` near the resolver callers. Install-local's uninstall guard and pair-door text only answer a declared 4xx, which is now consistent for a cycle. No source caller matches the old message.
- **Spec face:** one `ERROR_CODE_LEDGER` row, `CYCLIC_ARTIFACT_PACKAGES`, under `@objectstack/core`. The three regenerated docs differ only by `+368 more` → `+369 more` and the added bullet.
- **Tests:**
  - `...resolver-refusal-real-runtime.test.ts` (new) boots the real runtime and asserts that `collectJobsWithoutBody` is present. It covers three refusals, each checked with `expectNothingWritten`: no register call, no manifest-source entry, and `planDeclaredRenames` never called. It also has a 200 control.
  - The three forced test moves are each named in the body and match the diff.
  - The core tests pin the path through an optional edge, outsiders skipped, an external dependency ignored, and the unchanged message with no `code`.
- **Deviation, accepted:** `dev-i18n-packages-reader.test.ts` drops a `⛔ NO driver-memory mock here` comment and adds the absent-module `vi.mock`, with a census ledger row whose axis is `mock-replacement`.
  - The removed comment's premise was that a mock would make the file a third test consumer. But the census's closed vocabulary defines `mock-replacement` as "the real driver is never loaded here", which is not a ruled consumer.
  - `main` already carries 10 such rows, 4 of them in this same package (`dev-plugin*.test.ts`).
  - The edit is forced by `check:test-source-alias` on an edited test, and the area named it up front.
  - Recorded so L2 sees it; no change asked.
- **Gates at this head:** check-runs on `8490dc5d…`: 72 runs, 60 `success`, 12 `skipped`, 0 failed. The report's 54 predates the re-runs. `git merge-tree --write-tree` against today's `origin/main` is clean. `check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 34708`, read here: `NOT governed`, 0 of 17 paths, 548 lines.

### Residual (code-read, no change asked)

- The changeset bumps `@objectstack/spec` as `patch` for a new public error code. That is consistent with the ledger's additive rows; I only note it for the contract tier.

### Owed after this

- **L2: owed, `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`.** Spec face: a non-test `packages/spec/src` row in the error-code ledger. Also `Clause-②: yes` and the new core export `PluginOrderCycleError`.
- **Landing tier: spec face, handed to the seat for Tier H** (seat rule of 03:21Z). Not governed.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `8490dc5d22e034f0a368bc3f89d10d6b0bdfcf88`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts + packages/core/src/artifact-packages.ts, packages/core/src/plugin-order.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-dev/src/dev-i18n.ts (jsdoc), packages/runtime/src/artifact-collections.ts (jsdoc)

Inputs read: card #34574 body and all 7 comments (claim 6939731523, amendments 6939909352 and 6941981971, the three dev reports), PR #34708 body, its 17-file list and 3 comments, the net diff against merge-base `2e29287b9`, and the 72 check-runs on this head: every one completed, each `success` or `skipped`, none failed, none pending. The remaining 11 paths (tests, changeset, three generated reference pages, the census ledger) are the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Refusal vocabulary widens by one code: right.** `CYCLIC_ARTIFACT_PACKAGES` joins `ERROR_CODE_LEDGER['@objectstack/core']`, so `ErrorCode`, `ApiErrorSchema.code` and `FlowInnerRefusal.code` each accept one more member. The stamp site is `refuse()` in `packages/core/src/artifact-packages.ts`, inside the owner key that lists it, which is what the provenance rule in the ledger header asks.
- **A package cycle moves from a bare `Error` to a typed refusal at every reader: right.** The change is made once, in `resolveArtifactPackageEntries`, so every caller of it, of `resolveArtifactPackageOrder`, of `resolveStackCollection` and of the runtime's `resolveArtifactCollections` sees `code: 'CYCLIC_ARTIFACT_PACKAGES'`, `status: 422`, `details.cycle` (cli namespace utils, metadata, objectql's `manifest` service and reload, plugin-dev, plugin-security, runtime, verify). The verdict itself is unchanged: the sorter refused the same inputs before, self-dependency included.
- **No previously accepted input is refused: right.** `resolvePluginOrder` changes only the class of the value it throws and tracks a `path` array beside the existing `visiting` set; ordering and the set of refused graphs are untouched. The install-local change converts a throw into an answer and adds no new judgement.
- **install-local, real runtime: three sibling refusals and the cycle move from `500 INTERNAL_ERROR` to their own `422`: right.** The transport cannot do this itself: `declaredEnvelopeForThrow` renders only a status that is a key of `HttpStatusErrorCodeMap`, and 422 is not one, so a thrown 422 falls to the bare 500. The door has to answer.
- **The new catch reclassifies nothing: right.** `declaredRefusalAnswer` answers only a throw that itself declares a status below 500, with that throw's own status and its own registered code; an undeclared throw (a `TypeError`, a `ZodError` with no status) and any declared 5xx are rethrown unchanged. The sentence it appends, that nothing was installed or written, is true at this position: the unrunnable-code step precedes the conflict check, the datasource step, the hot-register and the ledger write. A side effect, stated because it is wider than the card: any other declared 4xx thrown out of the runtime binder's judgements at that step (for example `MIXED_ARTIFACT_COLLECTION_SHAPE`) is now also answered as itself instead of a 500. That is the same rule, and the right answer.
- **`declaredRefusalAnswer` forwards the refusal's own `details` on all four steps that use it: right, and a widening.** The envelope from steps 2a, 2b and 2c″ may now carry `details` where it carried `code` and `message` only. It is read only when it is a plain object; `ApiErrorSchema.details` is `z.unknown().optional()`, so the envelope still parses.
- **New public export `PluginOrderCycleError` from `@objectstack/core`: right.** `packages/core/src/index.ts` already re-exports `./plugin-order.js` whole, so the class is on the package index. It extends `Error`, keeps the message `[Kernel] Circular dependency detected: NAME` byte for byte, and carries no `code` and no `status`. The absent `code` is the correct reading of the #16404 rule in the ledger header (a `code` that ships in `dist` owes a row): the sorter mints no vocabulary, and the one mapping to the ledger code is the `instanceof` branch in `resolveArtifactPackageEntries`. Kernel boot (`kernel.ts`, `kernel-base.ts`) and `orderHydrationBatch` call the sorter directly and none of them reads a `code`.
- **`ArtifactPackageError` gains an optional `details`: right**, additive on an exported type.
- **Generated reference pages match the ledger.** `error-code-ledger.mdx`, `contract.mdx` and `automation-api.mdx` each gain the one member in alphabetical position, and the two enum summaries move from `+368 more` to `+369 more`. No other page in the diff restates the list.
- **Doors, asked one by one.** install-local: answered at the unrunnable-code step, and at 2a, 2b and 2c″ for a runtime that carries no judgements. Plugin order at kernel boot: no HTTP door, the typed error is the boundary. Runtime `resolveArtifactCollections` and the plugin-dev i18n reader: boot and dev-boot readers with no HTTP door of their own; both now throw the typed refusal and both docblocks say so. objectql's `manifest` service: reached from install-local only after the steps above, and its reload path catches and logs. I found no HTTP door on this tree that still answers `500 INTERNAL_ERROR` for a package cycle under the runtime the repo ships.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: yes (widening) — correct. The ledger header rules that registering a code widens the published error-code face, and the new export widens `@objectstack/core`. The line is present in the PR body and in the changeset body, with `Metadata-protocol: none`.

`Metadata-protocol: none` is right: nothing a metadata author can write is added, removed or re-read; a cyclic artifact was refused before and is refused now. Under AGENTS.md Post-Task step 3 the level follows the kind alone, and `none` takes `patch`. The changeset carries `patch` for `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/cloud-connection`, the three packages whose behaviour or vocabulary moves. No BREAKING banner is owed: nothing is removed or renamed, and the changeset says a caller matching the old message still finds `Circular dependency detected`.

`@objectstack/plugin-dev` and `@objectstack/runtime` move by docblock only and carry no changeset entry. The corrected `@throws` text does ship in their declaration files, but the behaviour it describes is published by core and stated in core's entry. Accepted as the lane's call; `Check Changeset` is green on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev flag, report 6939868658 (`needs_decision`: no registered code fits a cycle): answered by the seat's naming ruling relayed in amendment 6939909352, which also moved the declaration to `Clause-②: yes (widening)`. The name is the seat's call and is not judged here.
- Dev flag, report 6941957403 (`blocked`: `check:driver-memory-census` red, remedy outside the surface): answered by amendment 6941981971. The ledger row is the `mock-replacement` axis the ledger itself defines for a `vi.mock` factory, it names the one test file whose mock this diff adds, and the factory in the diff throws not-found as the row says. The census is hand-edited by its own rule, not generated; the row is the whole change to that file.
- Dev flag, same report (`marketplace-install-local-namespace-gate-33922.test.ts` outside the surface): answered by the same amendment as a forced move; lane remainder.
- Dev flag, report 6942992832 (PR body patch refused by the relay): closed. The PR body on this head carries the prepared text and the signed trailer.
- `open_questions`: none in any report.
- Governed surface: none of the 17 paths is on the governed register (instruction files, skills, ADR surfaces), and `Governed Surface Queue Guard` is green on this head. The contract tier is owed by the published-schema face alone.
- SQL push-down: not applicable. The diff adds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join; the only new data structure is the sorter's in-memory visit path.
- Docs Drift Check (advisory, comment 6941969340): the hand-written pages it lists name `ERROR_CODE_LEDGER`, the install-local route or `resolvePluginOrder`. I read the ones that discuss these refusals (`content/docs/plugins/packages.mdx`, `content/docs/protocol/kernel/plugin-spec.mdx`): neither states that an artifact cycle is a bare error, and the kernel boot message plugin-spec quotes is unchanged. Nothing is falsified.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

**`packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts`** — against the ruling it implements (amendment 6939909352, ADR-0130 D5) and its first consumer (`declaredRefusalAnswer` on install-local).

- Needed: yes. The standard catalog has no member for "packages that cannot be ordered", and the three siblings each carry their own registered code at 422; a cycle answered under a sibling's code would mis-state the fault, and under the status-derived member would lose the specific code. The synonym gate and the admission lint are green.
- Placed: under `@objectstack/core`, the package that stamps it, directly after its three siblings.
- Shaped: the comment states the status (`422`, stamped by `refuse()`), the `details.cycle` shape and its reading order, and the door. Each sentence agrees with the code at this head: edges are `manifest.dependencies` keys entered as the sorter's optional edges, the path is read off `PluginOrderCycleError.cycle`, and install-local forwards `details`.
- Tried to break: a cycle mixing hard and optional edges, a cycle reached past packages outside it, a dependency on a package the artifact does not carry, and a self-dependency all produce a path in edge order with the first id repeated last; `path` and `visiting` are pushed and popped together, so `path.indexOf` cannot miss. The `instanceof` test cannot fail across duplicate copies of core, because the throw and the catch are in one module graph. A non-cycle throw from the sorter is rethrown unchanged.

**`packages/core/src/plugin-order.ts`, `packages/core/src/artifact-packages.ts`** — agree with the ledger row and with their own docblocks, sentence by sentence. The module header's "never off a second walk of the graph" holds: the resolver reads the sorter's path and adds no second sort, which is what ADR-0130 D5 forbids. The refusal message keeps `Circular dependency detected`, so the two tests on main that match that phrase stay pinned.

**`packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts`** — the catch is the same three lines steps 2a, 2b and 2c″ already use, so the same bytes are answered alike whichever step reads them first, which is the function's stated contract. Judged under ① for what it can and cannot catch.

**`dev-i18n.ts`, `runtime/src/artifact-collections.ts`** — comment-only, and both now describe the behaviour the tree has.

Nits, none affecting correctness or the contract; all are prose in code files, so they are left as accepted deviations or a follow-up card, not fixed on this head:

- N1 (nit) — the ledger comment says "two or more of whose packages depend on each other". A package whose `manifest.dependencies` names itself is refused under the same code with `details.cycle` of `['a', 'a']` (pinned in `plugin-order.test.ts`), so one package suffices.
- N2 (nit) — the new row sits inside the group headed "The nine rows below are `door: 'none'` codes ... none reaches an HTTP door on this tree", and says "Door reading as the siblings", while the sibling paragraph directly above still records install-local answering with `PLUGIN_REGISTER_FAILED`. The new row's own reading is the true one. The sibling paragraph was already out of date on main (since #34407 and #34432), and this PR extends the siblings' reach to the real runtime. Worth a follow-up card that refreshes the group count and the sibling door reading in one pass.
- N3 (nit) — `declaredRefusalAnswer`'s docblock (and the new test's title) call the unrunnable-code step "1c". In the handler that step is labelled `1d`; `1c` is the ADR-0087 protocol handshake.
- N4 (nit) — `details.cycle` reaches the wire because `declaredRefusalAnswer` reads `err.details` itself. The shared `resolveThrownHttpError` does not read a thrown `details`, so a future door answering this refusal through the shared resolver would carry the code and status without the cycle. No such door exists on this tree. Recorded for whoever adds one.
